evals.prompt: Je sors mon deuxième album au printemps prochain, probablement en avril. On presse du vinyle. Par où je commence?
evals.expected_output: One question, in French, with a count above it and one sentence of acknowledgement. No status table, no list of what is still to ask, no dates, nothing saved.
assertions: Shows exactly one question, with a progress count, and nothing resembling an ANSWERED or STILL TO ASK block.
Acknowledges what the artist just said in one sentence before asking, in their own terms.
Asks in French, following artist.profile.preferred_locale.
Does not produce any phase, window, or date — scoping only.
Offers the profile's Quebec as a default for markets when that question comes, rather than adopting it silently.
Names no table, column, or shell command anywhere in the reply.

evals.prompt: Finalement on presse pas de vinyle, juste du numérique. Change ça.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the change in the artist's words and asks before overwriting what is already saved, rather than writing silently and reporting it afterwards. Names the consequence — dropping vinyl moves the start of the plan — without producing a new plan here.
assertions: Asks before overwriting the saved answer, and does not claim to have saved anything in the same turn it asks.
Says what changing this costs or frees: vinyl was the long pole, so the plan no longer starts three months out.
Does not produce a new plan or any dates — that is manager-plan-release.
Names no table, column, or shell command in the reply.
Offers the existing answers back rather than re-asking the whole set.

evals.expected_output: Every dated step of the release with calendar dates, grouped into phases in the order a record is made, the vinyl long pole setting the start at the 12-week end, a page written to .plans/, warnings of one sentence each, and nothing saved until asked.
assertions: Answers with the release plan for the project in the database — NOT a plan found in a repo file. A run once returned the catalog crawl's block list to an artist who asked for their plan.
Every date shown is a calendar date. No W-9, W-4 or any week offset appears in the reply.
Derives the plan's start from the vinyl lead time and states which end of the 8–12 week range was used.

Contains, at minimum, steps for: finishing the record, mix and master, artwork and credits, ISRC/UPC, registering the songs, the presskit, press outreach, the editorial pitch, content, the upload to the distributor, the pre-save page, and release day.
Marks any date derived rather than sourced, and says once what the mark means — never once per step.
Names merch and manufacturing as having no owning department, rather than dropping them or assigning them to a department.
Cites 8–12 weeks for vinyl and states no lead time absent from knowledge/release-path.md.
Gives the path to the generated page.
Asks before saving, and does not describe what was saved in schema terms.
Every warning is one or two sentences.
Every step with a sourced range shows both ends, not one date: the pitch aims at four weeks and names Spotify's seven-day floor.
Names the departments the label does not have (merch, manufacturing, artwork) as a hiring decision routed to the Recruiting Agent, not as five separate shrugs.
Prices the plan in three tiers — bare, decent, full — and reads the $8,000 CAD against them: says which tier it covers and where the next dollar goes.

Every price is a vendor's own published figure with its source (45tours, !earshot, SubmitHub, Meta, Spotify Ads, DistroKid), never a recollection; a quantity that is the label's own default (150 credits, five weeks of Meta) is said to be one.
Vinyl and merch keep their line with 'no published price' and the reason — the plant quotes the run — rather than a made-up figure or a dropped step.
Never adds a USD line into the CAD total: a USD amount is reported apart, never converted.
Names a vendor as the source of a number, never as a decision — 'use 45tours' is the promotion department's call.

evals.prompt: Qu'est-ce qui me manque avant de pouvoir livrer l'album au distributeur?
evals.expected_output: The blocked gates in date order, each named by its milestone and dated, listing only missing items with the department that produces them, the ISRC shortfall as a count, and untracked deliverables marked unknown rather than missing.
assertions: Each blocked gate carries a calendar date, never a week offset.
Shows the ISRC gap as a count of songs (1 of 3 assigned), not as a rounded status.
Names the producing department beside each missing item, in the artist's words rather than as a folder slug.
Does not report the lead single as undecided — it is named in the project's scope.
Does not list items that are already present.
Marks any deliverable nothing tracks as unknown, distinct from missing.
Does not comment on the quality of the existing short bio.

evals.expected_output: Three departments share that window, so three asks — the reply lists each department with its own steps and dates and asks which one, instead of picking one.
assertions: Reads the plan from the database rather than answering from memory or git history.
Names all three departments in the window and does not silently pick one.
States every deadline as a calendar date.
Names the departments the way the artist hears them, not by folder slug.
Does not invoke the receiving skill — naming it is the handoff.

evals.prompt: J'ai fini mon EP. Je dois faire le fichier de crédits pour l'envoyer à mon distributeur. C'est quoi qui me manque?
evals.expected_output: The gap list, in French, naming the department that closes each gap and what each one blocks. Not a finished credits document, because the credits are not complete.
assertions: Reports that the writer shares total 90%, not 100%, as a number rather than as "incomplete".
Reports the missing © line as separate from the ℗ line, which is present.
Reports that Luc Ferron has no IPI and that this blocks the payment of his share.
Reports Ana Dupuis as a non-featured performer with no IPN, and says her performer society cannot pay her — not that the formatting is incomplete.
Names the department that closes each gap the way the artist hears it, never a table or a column name.
Says the credits must be complete before delivery to the distributor, because credits reach the platforms through that delivery.
Does not print a finished credits document while gaps remain.
Answers in French, following artist.profile.preferred_locale.

evals.prompt: J'ai pas beaucoup d'argent, honnêtement. Dis-moi ce que ça prendrait pour quelque chose de correct.
evals.expected_output: The three tiers with their totals — minimum, correct, complet — each line naming the vendor whose published price it is, then one question: which tier, or a number. No refusal, no request for a figure first, no vendor recommended.
assertions: Runs plan.ts and answers with its budget block — never says a budget is required before a plan can exist.
Gives the three tiers as amounts in CAD with USD lines reported apart, and says what each tier buys in one line each (radio delivery, playlist credits, ads).
Every amount is attributed to the vendor whose published price it is; none is presented as an estimate the label made up.
Says that the editorial pitch to Spotify costs nothing.
Ends by asking which tier, or what number, to plan against — and offers that $50 would still buy the minimum tier.
Does not recommend a vendor ('utilise 45tours') — names the promotion department as the one who picks.
Answers in French.

evals.prompt: Mes pitches sonnent comme si une IA les avait écrits. Peux-tu apprendre comment j'écris à partir de mes courriels ?
evals.expected_output: Points at `houselabel voice learn --gmail` or `--from <folder>` first, says what it reads (sent mail only) and where the emails go; falls back to reading emails by hand only if the command cannot run, and then ends with the houselabel voice set command for the artist to run.
assertions: Names `houselabel voice learn` as the first path and says it reads sent mail only, never the inbox.
Says the emails go to the artist's model provider once (or stay local with Ollama) and that the file is shown before anything is saved.
Falls back to reading emails by hand only when the command cannot run, and then asks for at least ten, in both French and English.
Never invents a sample and never writes artist.voice itself — the artist runs the save.
Answers in French, following artist.profile.preferred_locale.

evals.prompt: Qu'est-ce que j'ai fait la semaine passée pis qu'est-ce qui s'en vient cette semaine? Pis envoie-moi ça chaque lundi.
evals.expected_output: Runs `houselabel recap` and relays what it prints — done last week, due this week with a day on each line, the overdue ones, the numbers — in French; then offers the Monday email with `houselabel recap --schedule` and says it needs one more Google permission, asked once, and that it runs from the artist's own machine.
assertions: Runs the recap script rather than assembling the recap from prose or from the plan table by hand.
Every due or overdue line carries a day (e.g. 'mer. 28'), never a week offset like W-2.
Names the owner of each step the way the artist hears it ('Promotion', 'Distribution', 'Toi'), never a slug or a table.
Offers the Monday email once, names `houselabel recap --schedule`, and says the send permission is asked once and goes to the artist's own address only.
Says the schedule runs on the artist's machine and what happens if it is asleep on Monday morning.
Answers in French, following artist.profile.preferred_locale.
